headline: Hugging Face shrinks AI search models, keeping accuracy
dek: The method keeps nearly all search quality, per Hugging Face.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: What happened
body: Hugging Face published a method that cuts the storage of multi-vector search models, per the company.
At 4x compression, the model kept 97.8% of its original quality, versus 94.6% for conventional training (Hugging Face).

s4.title: Why it matters
body: Multi-vector models search better but need lots of space: millions of documents produce hundreds of millions of vectors (Hugging Face).
With 4-bit quantization, cutting 200 vectors per document to 50 drops 12.8 GB to 3.2 GB (Hugging Face).

caption.hook: Hugging Face showed how to compress AI search models while losing almost no accuracy.
body: Multi-vector search models store a representation for every word in a document. That makes retrieval more precise, but per Hugging Face, a corpus with millions of documents can produce hundreds of millions of vectors.

The company published pooling-aware training, which trains the model knowing it will be compressed later. Per Hugging Face, at 4x compression the model kept 97.8% of its search quality, versus 94.6% for a conventionally trained model. The method was published on November 11, with open code, for users of the Sentence Transformers library.
